title: Tensor Orthogonal Subspace Split: Theory and Applications
summary: Tensor representations have emerged as a fundamental paradigm for modeling multidimensional data by preserving intrinsic correlations across multiple modes. This paper proposes a novel theoretical framework, termed Tensor Orthogonal Subspace Split (TOSS), which explicitly splits a tensor, along a prescribed mode, into two orthogonal components: a dominant component lying in a prescribed subspace and a residual component lying in the corresponding orthogonal complement.
